title: 1954 AHSME Problem 35
statement: In the right triangle shown the sum of the distances \(\overline{BM}\) and \(\overline{MA}\) is equal to the sum of the distances \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{CA}.\) If \(\overline{MB}=x,\) \(\overline{CB}=h,\) and \(\overline{CA}=d,\) then \(x\) equals:

solutions.text:
The condition and the Pythagorean theorem give \[ x+\sqrt{d^2+(h+x)^2}=h+d. \] After isolating the radical and squaring, \[ d^2+(h+x)^2=(h+d-x)^2. \] Cancelling common terms leaves \[ 4hx+2dx=2hd, \] so \(x=\frac{hd}{2h+d}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
